# Saved searches

The `SavedSearchSubscription` handler pushes the `facetState` of the SRP into the Alerthub digest queue.

Current as of: 2026-10-12 · 4e1c9ab

## Why
Buyers re-run the same SRP filters every day, and the PDP funnel loses them to the Alerthub cron before they see a new listing. Saved searches keep the filters and send new matches by email.

## What it does
- The Save search button on the results page stores the current filters under the buyer's account.
- The digest toggle switches the daily email on or off for one saved search.
- A buyer can keep at most 20 saved searches; the 21st attempt shows the limit message.

**Does not do:** push notifications, sharing a saved search with another buyer.

## How it works
The button calls `POST /api/v2/saved-searches` with the `facetState` from `useSearchFilters()` (`src/search/useSearchFilters.ts:42`). The handler writes the row and puts a `saved_search_cron` job into `digestQueue`; `dedupe_hash` is the SHA-1 of the sorted filters and keeps two identical searches from becoming two jobs.

## Code
| Layer | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| API | `src/api/savedSearches.ts` | creates and deletes a saved search |
| Store | `src/search/savedSearchStore.ts` | holds the list for the account page |

## Watch out
If you change the `savedSearches` store contract, run the whole search flow: 17 files read the store.

- Mechanics: POST /api/v2/saved-searches takes facetState from useSearchFilters(); the handler writes a row and enqueues a saved_search_cron job into digestQueue; dedupe_hash is the SHA-1 of the sorted filters.
- Dangerous: the savedSearches store is read by 17 files; changing its contract breaks the whole search flow.
- Code: src/api/savedSearches.ts creates and deletes; src/search/savedSearchStore.ts holds the list for the account page.
